races.name: William Hill Extra Place Races Daily Handicap

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Michael Dods who has visited the frame twice from 15 recent similar-going runs; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence, and at age 8 his ability to reproduce his best is the key question, but he is structurally gifted by having no genuine rival for the lead here.

runners_data.name: Pellitory
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4-year-old has raced prominently in all recent 7f Good-ground starts and Tudhope is a significant booking, but a form string of 550-00 offers little encouragement that a win is imminent even from a handy position.

runners_data.name: Yanifer
runners_data.note: Harriet Bethell's 8-year-old has placed twice on soft ground over course and distance, but only 7 of 15 similar-going runs have delivered competitive efforts; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is a positive, and the horse has genuine form at this trip.

runners_data.name: Croupier
runners_data.note: Joel Parkinson and Sue Smith's 7-year-old has three career wins and five places at similar going, including wins at 7f-8f Good, but 57 days off and a trainer strike rate of 0/4 over 14 days tempers enthusiasm; David Nolan knows this horse well.

runners_data.name: Morte Point
runners_data.note: William Muir & Chris Grassick's 4-year-old is at heart a front-running type — hg:b headgear suggests the stable is trying to channel its natural enthusiasm — but with several horses ahead of it in the queue for early position, it is unlikely to reproduce conditions similar to its win; shown in midfield on the map because it simply cannot get to the front in this field.

runners_data.name: Angel Hunter
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 4-year-old carries the hood again and has one win at 8f on good ground, but five of the six most recent efforts in the 6-8 range suggest this trip is functional rather than ideal; Joe Leavy has limited opportunities to make an impact from a prominent draw.

runners_data.name: Goldmoyne
runners_data.note: James Owen's 6-year-old has consecutive seconds at 7f Good, giving a solid profile of consistent prominence without winning; Cieren Fallon is the key booking, only 6 days since last run is worth monitoring, but the horse's pattern suggests it produces its best when racing handy on quick ground.

runners_data.name: Wild Nature
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 4-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer who won over 7f on Standard ground and placed at 7f Good; Oisin Orr takes the ride and 13 days since last run is fine, though the horse needs something to happen in front to produce a late effort.

runners_data.name: Milford
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 4-year-old is a hold-up type who has shown four placings on Good to Firm-type ground at distances shorter than today's 7f; the step back up in trip could help, and Bishop's placing record on this horse is reasonable, though a win has been elusive across 15 similar-going runs.

runners_data.name: Lir Speciale
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 7-year-old has four placings from recent 7f-8f Good-ground runs without winning, and Ben Robinson takes the ride; the horse's style suits a moderate gallop where it can travel prominently off the pace and sustain its effort through the final 2f.

runners_data.name: Our Havana
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's 5-year-old won over this exact trip on Good ground last time out, and Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim makes the weight attractive; three course-and-distance victories in similar going highlight this as a horse whose profile squarely fits today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Tilted Kilt
runners_data.note: William Knight's 4-year-old is a hold-up performer wearing the hood, who won over 8f on Standard ground; dropping to 7f is a slight concern given the history at slightly longer trips, and Hector Crouch will need a strong pace to unfold late.

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 4-year-old is genuinely drawn to race up with the pace — two wins at 6f Good underscore how keen it wants to be prominent — but in a 19-runner field overloaded with pace-lovers, it is mapped to midfield because the position simply is not available; Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a positive if it can find any rhythm.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's 4-year-old has three wins and three places at similar going, including a recent win at 7f Soft; the hood is off now, and Finley Marsh rides in a race where a moderate gallop may not suit a horse who has often needed a good pace to reel in rivals.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's 4-year-old has back-to-back seconds over 7f-8f Good ground and wears the tongue-pin; Kevin Stott is an astute booking and the horse's consistency — four places from five recent similar-going runs — marks it as a genuine contender if the pace develops enough to let it close from midfield.

runners_data.name: King Casper
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's horse returns from a 287-day absence, which is the single biggest flag in the race; showed promise at 2 with two wins and two places at 8f Good, and Cam Hardie partners, but fitness on comeback is the obvious unknown and the shorter trip is unproven.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5-year-old is a true hold-up performer who has placed three times over 7f Good and carries strong in-form trainer credentials (T14: 16/98); mapped to midfield due to redistribution, but in reality David Allan will be looking for a late run — the race needs to truly develop for Son to pick up.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's 4-year-old is at heart a horse that settles well and produces late, with a win at 8f Good and consistent place form; like Son, it is mapped to midfield because genuine hold-up types are numerous in this field, but Kieran O'Neill will be patient and hoping the pace scenario loosens up the race.

runners_data.name: Quest For Fun
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 8-year-old is a natural prominent type who has placed twice at 7f Good and shown consistent form in similar conditions, but with three rivals ahead of it fighting for front-rank positions, Duran Fentiman will find it impossible to replicate those conditions; the STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful here.

races.paceDynamic: Northern Express is the one confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, faces no genuine rival who will push him hard from the outset — Good To Firm ground at York over 7f suits a horse who can dictate his own rhythm and control sectionals from the front. The displaced prominent types — Morte Point, Lord Roxby, and Quest For Fun — are true pace-lovers who cannot all find their natural berth in a 19-runner field this pace-rich, meaning some will be shuffled wider or further back than ideal, softening the early pressure on Northern Express. Pellitory, Yanifer, Croupier, and Goldmoyne will race handy but none is a natural front-runner, so the gallop is unlikely to be truly searching; a controlled, even pace plays directly into the hands of horses travelling prominently or just off the pace who can produce a sustained run from 2f out rather than a late sprint. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the handy, prominent, or mid-division types who travel well within themselves and have the tactical speed to pounce in the straight — pure hold-up closers are structurally disadvantaged when the pace is moderate and the gaps may not materialise late. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position; Northern Express is best placed to lead, with Goldmoyne and Pellitory likely to claim the prime early slots just behind, while Morte Point, Lord Roxby, and Quest For Fun are most likely to find themselves shuffled wider and racing out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent stalkers travel smoothly before unleashing sustained finishes from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Northern Express sets a comfortable tempo on Good To Firm ground and is never seriously threatened for the lead, leaving the handy horses ideally placed to peel off him turning in; horses like Goldmoyne, Our Havana, and Lir Speciale — who travel prominently and have strong 7f York-type form — are perfectly set up to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Closers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the fractious redistribution of prominent types causes enough early jostling that the gallop is faster than expected, stretching the field and opening a lane for the hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: With multiple horses fighting for prominent positions, the early sections become stronger than anticipated, and a genuine searching gallop sets up horses who can produce a late burst; Andesite, Rare Change, and Wild Nature — genuine hold-up types with good recent form — are the profile here, having the stamina and finishing kick to benefit from a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express gets an easy lead and the moderate pace lasts long enough that no prominent horse can close him down in the straight.
scenarios.body: On a flat, fast York 7f, a horse given a soft lead and a positive ride can simply outstay rivals who are taken off the bridle too late; Northern Express, though showing STYLE_FIT caution, has obvious claims if allowed to roll along at his own pace and the chasing pack is fractionally slow to respond turning for home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Movers, Chaos Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field produces significant traffic trouble or a wide draw forces key fancied horses into problematic positions, scrambling the expected race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Horses drawn widest and forced to cover extra ground are disadvantaged on a flat track at York in a big field, while those who find a clean passage regardless of early positioning become the beneficiaries; King Casper, returning from 287 days off but with a Hugo Palmer angle, and Son, a true hold-up type with consistent 7f form, represent the chaos-beneficiary profile if the race falls apart tactically.

watchPoints.text: Northern Express (front-runner) has no genuine rival for the lead — if Paul Mulrennan gets a soft split from stall and dictates every fraction, prominent stalkers like Goldmoyne and Our Havana must time their challenge perfectly or risk being held at bay.

Morte Point, Lord Roxby, and Quest For Fun are all natural pace-lovers who cannot all find their favoured position in this 19-runner field — watch for early jostling in the first 2f, particularly from wide draws, that could disrupt the pace map entirely.

Our Havana is the most recent winner in the race over course and distance on similar going, but Warren Fentiman (3lb claimer) has limited experience in large-field competitive handicaps at York — execution of the race plan will be critical.

King Casper returns from 287 days off for Hugo Palmer — watch market moves in the hour before post time, as Palmer often has his returning horses fit to run well, and any significant support would elevate this runner's significance.

Andesite has posted consecutive placed efforts over 7f-8f Good with Kevin Stott aboard and wearing the tongue-pin — if the pace scenario develops into a genuinely run race, this consistent performer could emerge as the most dangerous horse from the chasing pack.

races.name: William Hill Summer Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Group 3)

runners_data.name: Celandine
runners_data.note: Consistent recent form at 6f on Good ground (5th, 7th, 2nd in last three at the trip) makes her interesting, but she is a natural front-runner who will find herself shuffled back in this traffic-heavy field — her best chance depends on getting a cleaner run than the pace map allows.

runners_data.name: First Instinct
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained filly stepping back to 6f after a run of 5f efforts; Cieren Fallon booking is a plus and she handles Good ground, but her last five runs are all over the minimum trip and her prominent style may be hard to deploy with Flora Of Bermuda and America Queen also keen to be close.

runners_data.name: Flora Of Bermuda
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old is the standout course-and-distance performer in the field — her sole win came over this exact 6f York trip on Good ground and James Doyle rides; she is one of the few prominently-drawn horses with a genuine right to her early position in this race.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope rides a filly who has won twice but mostly over 5f, and her last run was an unseated-rider — she is a natural front-runner who will struggle to express that style in this busy field, and the step up to 6f adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Hold A Dream
runners_data.note: A 69-day absence is a notable flag for Clive Cox's filly; she has winning form at 6f on Good ground (2nd last time out) but the layoff, a modest trainer 14-day strike rate, and the fact she is a prominent type likely to find herself in midfield all suppress her chance here.

runners_data.name: Kinswoman
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners a Haggas filly whose best form is at 5f on soft going — most of her wins and places came in softer conditions, and the Good to Firm ground allied with a step up to 6f both look like concerns for a horse already displaced from her natural prominent position.

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's three-year-old has a perfect 5-from-5 record at this track-and-going combination, runs well fresh, and Paul Mulrennan is positive in style — she is one of the genuine candidates to take up a prominent role behind Spicy Marg and her 6f York form is as good as anything in this field.

runners_data.name: Catching The Moon
runners_data.note: Fahey's three-year-old has won over 5f and 6f on soft ground and comes here after an 83-day break — she has been nudged to the back of the pace map as a least pace-committed type, meaning she would need the race to fall apart in front of her, and the fast ground is an unknown factor.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's three-year-old (T14: 0/15) has not won in several outings and her best form is at 6-7f; she is a natural prominent racer unlikely to get her position in this field, and the trainer's current form column offers no encouragement for a win at this level.

runners_data.name: Fitzella
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly has been consistently placed at 6f on Good ground (five runs, all on similar going, all in the places), but her finishing positions have plateaued at fifth-to-sixth in recent outings — a true prominent racer who will be denied her natural position here, which further limits her ceiling.

runners_data.name: Royal Fixation
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old is equipped with hood/tp headgear and has a strong record at 6f on Good ground — two wins and two places from five similar-going attempts — and Sam James is a solid booking; one of the live candidates to sit prominently and get involved in the straight.

runners_data.name: Soul Love
runners_data.note: Burke's other runner in the race has won three of her last four and handles Good to Firm well enough, but a 69-day absence and the fact she has been mapped to the rear against her natural prominent style means her winning chance depends on a pace collapse that this race shape is unlikely to produce.

runners_data.name: Spicy Marg
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old is the one confirmed front-runner in the field — she has winning form at 6f on Good ground and Hector Crouch will look to control matters from the off; the style-fit tag is a minor caution but her tactical advantage of an uncontested lead is significant in this particular race.

races.paceDynamic: Spicy Marg is the one confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner Group 3 field and, with no serious challenger for the lead, she should dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at York — a track where a controlled pace over 6f often rewards those travelling prominently and kicking off the bend. The bulk of this field are natural prominent-racers, meaning Flora Of Bermuda, America Queen, First Instinct and Royal Fixation will all push forward to track Spicy Marg closely, creating a competitive but orderly pace rather than a suicidal burn. This field holds far more front-running and prominent types than the track can accommodate in those positions — Fitzella, Celandine, Hold A Dream, Fluorescence, Kinswoman and Figjam are all genuine prominent racers who will be squeezed back against their nature, with Flora Of Bermuda, America Queen and First Instinct most likely to actually secure the coveted early positions behind the leader. The race shape strongly favours horses who can sit in the first three or four and travel smoothly into the straight, rather than hold-up types trying to make ground on a track where late closers must overcome a course bias that leans toward prominent runners on fast ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Spicy Marg sets a controlled pace and the horses tracking her travel comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Flora Of Bermuda, America Queen and Royal Fixation can all sit within two lengths of the leader, get a clean run rounding the bend and sustain their effort on this fast ground to hit the line first — this is York 6f's textbook shape. Prominent, well-handled horses with Group-level form at this course and distance are the clear beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace unravels, strong closer
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of naturally prominent horses disrupts early order and produces a faster-than-anticipated pace.
scenarios.body: Should the crowded prominent group press Spicy Marg harder than expected, the pace could compromise several of them, opening a window for the horses pushed to the rear — Soul Love and Catching The Moon — to pick up ground late into the York straight. Neither is a natural hold-up type, however, and both would need the race to truly collapse in front of them to get involved.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner outstays field
scenarios.trigger: If Spicy Marg's uncontested lead allows her to dictate every yard and produce a strong staying effort at the business end.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to go with her early, Spicy Marg could set a perfectly judged fractions race, conserving enough energy to sprint clear in the final furlong before any challenger can reel her in — her Good to Firm form is solid and she is well-handled by Michael Bell. A wire-to-wire win from the front is a live scenario in a field where her natural rivals are all disadvantaged by the pace map.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed types find rails
scenarios.trigger: If a clean break allows one of the naturally prominent horses mapped to midfield to slot forward and find a good position early.
scenarios.body: Fitzella or Celandine, both true prominent racers artificially shown in midfield, could find themselves closer to the pace than the map suggests if gaps appear early — but their style-fit discounts and the sheer number of horses ahead of them make this the least likely winning shape. Any winner from this group would require notable circumstance rather than design.

watchPoints.text: Flora Of Bermuda and America Queen both need to take up positions directly behind Spicy Marg — if they clash for the same ground rounding the bend, one or both could be compromised and shift the outcome entirely.

Spicy Marg's uncontested lead is the pivot of the whole race shape — watch her early sectionals; if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, she becomes a genuine winning threat rather than simply a pace-setter.

Soul Love and Catching The Moon are both naturally prominent horses placed in the rear by the pace map — if either shows their true early speed off the stalls and finds a position closer to the pace, the odds on a late run landing have already gone.

Royal Fixation's headgear (hood/tp) is worth noting at the track — K.R. Burke runners equipped with cheekpieces or hoods at York often show improved focus in the straight, and her 6f Good-ground form profile makes her a quiet player if the race sets up for prominent types.

The 55-day layoff for Royal Fixation and 69-day breaks for both Hold A Dream and Soul Love mean three runners return from notable absences — watch the market moves close to post time for any significant support that might signal stable confidence.

races.name: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Laura Barry Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Luzon Heights
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner for William Knight, carrying top weight off a 14-day turnaround; has finished placed twice at this trip on good ground and gets a perfect opportunity to control the race from the front, though the [STYLE_FIT] flag — technically mapped as prominent — reminds that fully dominating from the lead is a slight stretch beyond its usual role.

runners_data.name: Get Outta Here
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's 3yo arrives off a 21-day break with a recent York win at this exact trip and distance on good ground — his form profile is tailor-made for this course, and Hector Crouch is an astute booking for a horse that travels prominently and finishes well.

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's runner is rock solid on good ground with seven runs on that surface and a win over seven furlongs at York already on his CV; stepping up to the mile is the question, but Kevin Stott's course knowledge and a 3/11 trainer strike rate over 14 days adds appeal.

runners_data.name: Bee Farmer
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell, who has been in very good form this season, sends out this 3yo with just three runs to his name; the 7/8f good ground second on his last York visit is the obvious form link, though he remains unexposed and Oisin Orr's 3/23 trainer record is modest.

runners_data.name: Spectical
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's runner arrives with a blinker for the first time and has shown little on similar ground so far, with a 0-from-3 record on going in this range; James Doyle's booking maintains interest but the form says this represents a significant step up needed.

runners_data.name: Hambelton
runners_data.note: David Marnane has a quiet recent record (0/13 over 14 days) and this 3yo's sole win came on good ground at this trip, which is a positive; however, as a natural prominent runner with nowhere to go in a field stacked with pace-inclined rivals, it is likely to race further off the pace than it would prefer — a real structural problem.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the ride for Gemma Tutty on a hold-up horse that has struggled badly in recent starts, running 7th in five of its last eight outings at seven furlongs on good ground; the step up to a mile is a potential key, but the consistent poor finishes are hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Forest Phoenix
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's runner carries a ⚠ finish-fade flag and that is consistent with a profile showing a single win over five furlongs; David Allan takes the ride but stepping up to a mile on fast ground after a string of mid-field finishes at shorter trips is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope — a course specialist — rides a horse whose natural game is to race prominently, but the crowded pace landscape means Napolian is likely to find itself racing in midfield rather than its preferred spot; its recent win at this trip on good ground counts, but the positional squeeze tempers expectations meaningfully.

runners_data.name: Milford Grange
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty's mount has been a model of consistency, recording four placed finishes in its last five starts, though almost exclusively on soft ground — this good to firm surface represents a genuine concern and is the single biggest flag against it today.

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse with two recent wins in its armoury, Warren Fentiman (3) claims 3lb which helps the handicap mark; blinkers are fitted and it arrives off an 18-day break having won over both seven furlongs and a mile — but its simulated going record (8 from 10 runs, only 2W2P) flags that good-to-firm ground has historically not brought out its best.

races.paceDynamic: Luzon Heights is the confirmed lone front-runner and, with no genuine rival capable of pressing from the front, is set to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on good to firm ground over York's straight mile. Get Outta Here, Zarvali, and Bee Farmer will look to track prominently, but Hambelton and Napolian — both natural prominent types — are squeezed out of their preferred position by the volume of pace-inclined runners and will be forced to race closer to midfield than they would choose. The resulting shape is a single-file, measured early tempo that gradually quickens rather than blows up, meaning the race will be decided by a sustained pick-up in the final two furlongs rather than a dramatic late sprint. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind Luzon Heights and quicken off the back of a controlled pace — hold-up horses launching from deep are at a structural disadvantage given the lack of a truly fast early gallop to close into. Note that the field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate: of the redistributed trio, Luzon Heights is most likely to actually dictate, while Hambelton and Napolian are most likely to be shuffled back from their natural prominent roles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Luzon Heights sets a manageable tempo and the race unfolds at a steady-to-honest pace that suits horses tracking close behind.
scenarios.body: Luzon Heights dictates from the front and the prominent stalkers — Get Outta Here and Zarvali — travel smoothly in behind before being produced to challenge inside the final two furlongs; on good to firm York ground this is a textbook setup for horses settled just off the leader. Get Outta Here's recent win at this trip and Zarvali's strong course-form profile at the mile suit this shape best.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Luzon Heights is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged and the prominent stalkers fail to close the gap when the tempo lifts.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to press Luzon Heights, it conserves energy through a soft early pace and simply finds more in the straight when asked, with the chasing pack covering too much ground too late. This scenario suits William Knight's charge as the one confirmed front-runner benefiting directly from the structural setup of this race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is quicker than expected due to prominent horses jostling for position and the leaders tire in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Should the crowded prominent group create unintentional friction in the first half-mile, the early tempo rises enough to bring hold-up horses like Only Dream Big and Milford Grange — both with recent winning form — into the picture with a late rattle. Only Dream Big's two recent wins and Milford Grange's consistent placed form at this sort of trip give them each some credentials if the leaders come back to them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Split Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate and the race bunches turning into the straight, creating a wide-open finish with multiple closers finishing together.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish could see redistributed runners like Napolian and Hambelton — both genuine prominent types racing a touch further back than ideal — thread through a tiring field to grab a place or better. This is a lower-probability shape precisely because those runners are not in their natural positions and Spectical, unknown on this evidence, would need to step up markedly.

watchPoints.text: Hambelton and Napolian — both natural prominent types — will attempt to find a slot near the pace; watch the first furlong closely to see if they can press forward, as any scrimmaging for position in the prominent group could unintentionally push the tempo higher and alter the entire shape.

Only Dream Big arrives wearing blinkers for the first time and has the widest experience base of the hold-up horses, but its going record on fast ground is weak — if the track plays quicker than advertised the headgear effect may be neutralised.

Forest Phoenix has faded in finishes repeatedly and steps up sharply in trip today; if David Allan tries to place it prominently to compensate, it could contribute to an unbalanced early pace before weakening into the straight.

Milford Grange's form has been built entirely on soft or heavy ground — this is its first serious test on good to firm and Billy Garritty will need to be positive from the gates to ensure it does not get outpaced in a field where the leaders are likely to stride away on quick turf.

Spectical runs in blinkers for the first time for Andrew Balding, who has an excellent record freshening up horses with headgear changes — monitor early market moves to see if the yard expects a sharper performance than the form suggests.

races.name: Azets Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Prince Of The Seas
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for O'Meara and Tudhope, ran just seven days ago which bears watching for freshness, has placed at this trip on good ground (sim-going: 11 runs, 2 wins 4 places) and is well suited to a scenario where the pace is strong enough to close into.|

runners_data.name: Great Bedwyn
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type who has placed twice at 12f on good-to-firm equivalent ground, returns after 40 days off for Hannon which can be a positive angle, but his moderate sim-going record (7/15, 1W2P) and recent form string of 6-2828 suggest he needs things to fall perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Frankies Dream
runners_data.note: Natural 7-9f prominent performer stepping up to 1m2½f for Candlish — the style-fit flag and trip extension are both genuine concerns, and while Mulrennan should secure an uncontested lead, the question is whether the horse stays and sustains its effort once the race quickens in the home straight.|

runners_data.name: Dark Moon Rising
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who usually races off the pace but wears a prominent tag in his historical profile (hg:p suggests headgear change), Ryan's yard has had just one winner from 39 runners in 14 days suggesting muted stable form, and his recent finishing positions of 852450 are uninspiring.|

runners_data.name: Glistening Nights
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true racing style is further back than the map position suggests — the Fahey yard is in fair form (6/66 T14), and Glistening Nights has placed at 10f on good ground five times from 15 sim-going runs, but the redistribution into midfield means it may never settle where it wants to be.|

runners_data.name: Beach Point
runners_data.note: Naturally wants to race prominently for William Knight but the weight of pace runners in this field pushes it into a midfield role it does not prefer — the horse has placed at 10f on good ground six times in 15 attempts, and Hector Crouch will have to be patient rather than aggressive, which limits its natural profile.|

runners_data.name: Kahin
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for William Haggas and Cieren Fallon, both strong positives — won at 9f on good ground last time and has the profile of a progressive type stepping up in trip; prominent style should suit the race shape well if he handles the step to 1m2½f.|

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Donny
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby three-year-old who has placed four times from eight sim-going runs without winning — consistent but not a finisher, prominent style suits the likely race shape, and David Allan keeps rides simple, but the 0 wins from 6 similar-distance runs on good ground is a flag.|

runners_data.name: Bearin Up
runners_data.note: In-form three-year-old for Easterby with two wins and seven places from 13 sim-going runs — recent form of 731512 shows he bounced back to win last time, prominent style sits perfectly in this race shape, and 13 days since his last run looks ideal.|

runners_data.name: Ciao Capo
runners_data.note: Three wins from his last five starts give Ciao Capo strong form credentials and he has won at 10f on good ground, but his natural prominent style is congested out of position in this field — the redistribution onto the midfield map underplays what he naturally wants to do, and Hardie will need to decide early whether to push forward or accept the compromised berth.|

races.paceDynamic: Frankies Dream is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 10-runner field over 1m2½f on good-to-firm ground at York, and with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, Paul Mulrennan can dictate an unchallenged, sustainable gallop from the front. However, Frankies Dream is stepping up markedly in trip from its natural 7-9f comfort zone, and its style-fit tag flags that it is racing out of role — the horse may lead by default but may not be the dominant force it appears on paper. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all secure their preferred positions: Beach Point and Ciao Capo are both true prominent racers who will be squeezed back into midfield, while Glistening Nights is a genuine hold-up horse also mapped forward — Kahin, Stoneacre Donny, and Bearin Up are most likely to actually lock in the prominent berths behind the leader. With a single, uncontested front-runner setting a measured tempo over this trip on good-to-firm going, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can sit comfortably in the first three or four and produce a sustained run from two out — patient hold-up horses who need a strong pace to reel in leaders are at a disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Frankie Controls, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Frankies Dream bowls along uncontested at a fair but manageable pace and the prominent horses track closely enough to pounce in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Frankies Dream sets the fractions alone, the compact group of prominent types sits within striking distance, and the race develops into a sustained gallop that rewards those who have travelled well and can pick up off a steady tempo; the trip is the key variable for the leader, and those who have proven stamina at 10-12f on good ground are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Ranger Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Frankies Dream, operating on genuine good-to-firm ground and unchallenged for the lead, sets a slow enough tempo that the finish becomes a sprint finish favouring the front-runner.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to press, Mulrennan could steal a march on the field and the prominent horses fail to close in time, particularly if the ground rides faster than expected and the pace is deceptively quick early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Frankies Dream goes quick enough to string the field out and create the strong gallop that genuine hold-up horses require to finish through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Prince Of The Seas and Great Bedwyn are the true closers in this field, but their ability to get a run in a compressed finish at York depends on a genuinely strong tempo being set — Dark Moon Rising and Glistening Nights, who are also rearward types, benefit from the same scenario but their recent form is modest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Surprise Result
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent horses — Beach Point and Ciao Capo — disrupt the early order by pushing forward to claim their natural positions, creating a messy pace scenario.
scenarios.body: A scrambled early phase could unsettle Frankies Dream's rhythm and compress the field into a late cavalry charge where lower-weighted, well-handicapped runners get their chance; Ciao Capo has winning form over the trip and is dropping into a competitive mark, but its redistribution penalty limits confidence.

watchPoints.text: Kahin — Haggas and Fallon combination on a progressive three-year-old stepping up in trip; if he handles 1m2½f this runner could sit perfectly in the prominent pack and produce the strongest finish.|

Frankies Dream — monitor whether Mulrennan pushes forward immediately from the gate or allows rivals to press; any contest for the early lead will transform this race shape entirely and undermine the solo-leader scenario that underpins the dominant probability.|

Ciao Capo and Beach Point — watch the first two furlongs to see whether either pushes out of their mapped midfield positions to claim prominent ground; if both do, the early order becomes significantly more compressed than the map suggests.|

Bearin Up — Tim Easterby runners returning quickly (13 days) off a win can be vulnerable to handicapper's reassessment, but the strong sim-going profile and prominent style make this one worth tracking through the early part of the race for position.|

Prince Of The Seas — ran just seven days ago and is the most recent runner in the field; Tudhope is an astute judge of pace at York and will be watching to see if the tempo is strong enough to close from the rear in the final quarter-mile.|

races.name: William Hill Keep Your Raceday Positive Handicap

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Triton
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse for O'Meara and Tudhope, best form on good ground (won at 5f/GOO), will need a stronger-than-expected pace to get home from the back in a 5f straight sprint; headgear worn previously.

runners_data.name: Brazen Bolt
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who has placed at this course on good ground, held up by Fentiman, but trainer 0/32 in 14 days and recent form sketchy; needs a true pace to deliver his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Spring Is Sprung
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will try to dictate from the front; style-fit tag notes she is racing slightly out of optimal role in this shape, but as the only genuine pace-setter she has a clear positional advantage; consistent place record on fast ground.

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: In-form 4-year-old with two recent wins on good ground and consistent prominent style; Adam Kirby as trainer and Charles Bishop aboard, with headgear (t/ce) likely aiding focus — comfortably the most live prominent type once Spring Is Sprung goes clear.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6-year-old runs again quickly (7 days) which can suit fresh sprinters; ran 2nd on 5f/GOO most recently, goes prominently under a 5lb claimer, and her course and going form is solid at 3W5P in similar conditions.

runners_data.name: Al Hussar
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer on good ground with a win at 5f/GOO; headgear worn, Grant Tuer in 1/15 form over 14 days, and Oliver Stammers takes the ride — well positioned if he secures a forward berth in a competitive draw.

runners_data.name: Counsel
runners_data.note: Hold-up 8-year-old whose best turf form is on standard tracks; only 0W1P in similar going and the long flat York straight is not ideal for a horse who needs things to go his way; Whiteley 5lb claim is a help.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: Second trainer runner for Midgley alongside Spring Is Sprung; won at 5f/GOO recently, goes prominently, and David Nolan is an experienced partner — interesting place candidate if he settles just behind the pace battle.

runners_data.name: Castan
runners_data.note: Six-year-old held up by Mulrennan; 55 days off the track is a slight question, and only 0W2P in similar going on turf — needs a strong pace and clear passage in a 13-runner field to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Equity Law
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (1-2 in last three) on good ground and David Allan rides; though genuinely prominent in style, he has been redistributed to midfield here because more prominent types will crowd him out — his style-fit tag means his chance is tempered if he cannot get his natural early position.

runners_data.name: Muker
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse, true rear-runner pushed to midfield on the map because of congestion at the back; Tinkler's 1/23 fortnight strike rate is modest and recent York turf form is poor — would need a very strong gallop to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Rotokura Belle
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with two wins on good ground and solid form; naturally held-up but redistribution places her in midfield — Cam Hardie is a capable pilot and if she gets a clear run in the straight her finishing effort could be competitive, though style-fit tempers expectation.

runners_data.name: I'm Dan Dare
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old with recent winning form on good ground; Rhys Elliott 5lb claim, but he is a natural prominent type mapped to midfield because of overcrowding at the front — if he can reclaim any ground early the form makes him interesting, but the redistribution genuinely disadvantages him here.

races.paceDynamic: Spring Is Sprung is the one confirmed front-runner here, and on Good To Firm ground at York's straight 5f she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without being seriously harassed for the lead. The redistribution flags are significant: Equity Law, I'm Dan Dare, Ancient State, and Eternal Harmony are all genuine prominent-running types who cannot all slot into their natural position, meaning there will be scrapping for early berths that could stretch the pace more than Spring Is Sprung alone would suggest. Of those most likely to actually secure a prominent pitch, Ancient State (consistent near-side worker, in form) and Al Hussar look best placed to hold their ground, while Equity Law and I'm Dan Dare will likely be nudged further back than they want. The dominant shape here favours horses who can sit a length or two off the pace in a small group, travel fluently, and produce a clean turn-of-foot finish — making the in-form, prominent-to-mid types who secure good early positions the primary beneficiaries, rather than true hold-up horses who face a long, flat dig home in what is a processed, steady-to-honest gallop on fast ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Spring Is Sprung dictates a controlled, honest gallop and the prominent contingent settles in behind without a scramble blowing the race apart.
scenarios.body: Spring Is Sprung sets a measured tempo down the York straight, allowing horses in the first four or five to travel smoothly and produce their best into the final furlong; those with class and good form on fast ground are best positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Scramble Helps Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of prominent types causes a fierce early battle for position and the gallop is genuinely strong, compressing finishing positions.
scenarios.body: A hot pace set by multiple front-end types burns off Spring Is Sprung and stretches the field, leaving late runners with ground to make up but a genuinely run race to aim at; hold-up horses with good form on fast ground are the main beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Spring Is Sprung Wins It
scenarios.trigger: If Spring Is Sprung is totally unchallenged, the pace is very modest and she controls every yard to score.
scenarios.body: With no one willing to commit and push her along, she dictates a dawdle before quickening clear in the final furlong; horses with sharp acceleration who can quicken from just off the pace are the secondary winners if she gets run down late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffle Benefits Redistributed
scenarios.trigger: If the overall race shape collapses into a bunched-field sprint and horses mapped to midfield find an unexpectedly clear passage.
scenarios.body: The compressed nature of a 13-runner 5f sprint on fast ground occasionally produces a race where midfield becomes the sweet spot; redistributed types like I'm Dan Dare or Rotokura Belle, if they find racing room, could outrun their mapped position, though their style-fit tags temper confidence.

watchPoints.text: Ancient State and Al Hussar are both prominent-style types with good fast-ground form — watch how quickly they move to claim their early position as there may be a sharp battle for the rail or inside berth in the opening furlong.

Equity Law and I'm Dan Dare are both flagged as redistributed front-end types; if either finds a clear passage forward from the gates rather than being forced back, they immediately become more dangerous than the map position suggests.

Emerald Harmony runs for a second time in 7 days — watch her in the pre-race for signs of freshness or fatigue, as her chance is materially dependent on how she has recovered from the quick turnaround.

Spring Is Sprung's early stride pattern in the first two furlongs is the key pace barometer — if she is allowed to lope along unchallenged the race will be truly tactical; if Eternal Sunshine or Ancient State push her along the gallop becomes genuinely strong and hold-up horses improve in probability.

With 13 runners in a 5f straight sprint on Good To Firm ground, draw position and early crossing moves in the first 50 yards may create traffic for midfield horses — Rotokura Belle and Muker, already displaced from their natural rear position, are most vulnerable to losing further ground in the initial bunching.

races.name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Apprentice Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Golden West
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with 2W2P in similar going, best trip sits around 11-12f so this 14f trip is a slight stretch; Tim Easterby yard ticking over at 14/100 in 14 days and Jake Dickson carries 5lb claim, which helps offset the OR; has to be produced very late and needs more pace than this race is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Nightsinwhitesatin
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here and sole pace-setter, giving Horgan (3lb claim) complete control of the tempo; strong Good-ground profile at 12f (2W5P) and blinkers noted; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is mapped as a Prominent rather than confirmed leader — but uncontested she effectively reclaims that role and the 50-day break is the one query.

runners_data.name: Secret Beach
runners_data.note: Form has gone cold recently (7-5-9 last three) but retains a win at 12f on Good and Donald McCain is 1/10 in 14 days suggesting something is ticking; Warren Fentiman has limited big-field experience and the 10-runner field may create positional problems for a hold-up type from stall placement.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: The most eye-catching angle in the race — 645 days off the track (51 career hurdle starts) returning to flat company over a trip shorter than his recent jump efforts; Harry Fry's 3/4 14-day strike rate is significant and if fitness is there his Prominent style is well-suited to stalking a lone front-runner; the fitness doubt from such a lengthy absence remains the controlling factor.

runners_data.name: Humble Spark
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with four runner-up efforts in 15 starts in similar going, so consistent but a consistent loser; Jim Goldie yard modest at 7/44 in 14 days and Lauren Young's 3lb claim is a minor positive; needs a more searching pace than Nightsinwhitesatin is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Nicator
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's four-year-old has posted 0W1P in similar going but multiple places at 8-10f suggest the step to 14f is a new test; his Prominent style means he naturally gets a good tracking position and Taryn Langley's 3lb claim is useful; if the trip suits he is the most likely beneficiary of Scenario B.

runners_data.name: Optician
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Soft for Michael Herrington (3/18 in 14 days) and is a genuine hold-up type, but the redistribution into midfield is a real tactical concern — he is not a natural midfield horse and may find himself shuffled wider than ideal; Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim is an asset but the OR drop to 75 reflects modest current form.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Good last time (Rod Millman) and returns just 7 days later, suggesting connections are keen; a true hold-up horse repositioned toward midfield by the race shape, so Toby Moore (7lb claim) must overcome both positional compromise and the quick turnaround; the 0/21 trainer 14-day strike rate adds to the concern.

runners_data.name: Pleasant Man
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's eight-year-old has been placed four times at 12f on Good or Standard going, with a recent win at 12f; his Prominent style makes him the natural pace-stalker if Nightsinwhitesatin sets a steady tempo and Alex Jary (no claim) must ride him for the position from the start.

runners_data.name: Queen Roslyn
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with wins at 17f and 10f but form at this shorter trip on Good ground is thin; Brian Ellison is 1/20 in 14 days and Rhys Elliott's 3lb claim helps, but she is repositioned out of her natural hold-up role by the race shape and the OR of 62 (lowest in the field) reflects a significant class concession.

races.paceDynamic: Nightsinwhitesatin is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 1m4f handicap on Good to Firm ground at York, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Cian Horgan (3lb claim) can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured. Nicator and Pleasant Man will push to sit prominently just behind, creating a small lead group, but the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching given the absence of a pace rival. The field carries more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Optician, Green Sky, and Queen Roslyn are true closers that will be nudged toward midfield positions rather than their natural rearward slots, meaning the race may not set up as cleanly for late finishers as it might appear. This shape — a controlled single pace-setter, modest gallop, prominent/mid-division horses able to travel with cover — most strongly favours prominent to mid-division types that can chase down a front-runner who hasn't been truly tested early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nightsinwhitesatin Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Nightsinwhitesatin is allowed to dictate a steady pace without challenge and kicks clear in the straight, holding on under a positive Horgan ride.
scenarios.body: Bethell's mare has strong form at 12f on Good ground (2W5P in similar conditions) and, unopposed, can conserve energy through the first mile before asserting turning for home; her STYLE_FIT flag acknowledges she is racing out of her deepest comfort zone but the absence of a pace rival effectively restores that advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and a prominent tracker hits the front between 2f and 1f out when Nightsinwhitesatin's effort flattens.
scenarios.body: Pleasant Man's four consecutive placed efforts (including a win at 12f on Good) make him the archetypal pace-stalker who benefits from this shape; Nicator has also posted multiple runner-up efforts and handles Good ground, positioning him to pounce if the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough — or the lead group fights among themselves — to create a true stop-start gallop that leaves late ground for genuine closers.
scenarios.body: Golden West has the best course-form profile of the hold-up brigade (placed at 11f on Good) and Humble Spark has posted multiple 2nd finishes at 11-13f on Good ground, giving both a chance if the race is truly run to suit; however, Optician, Green Sky and Queen Roslyn's redistribution flags mean the anticipated late-running pool is diluted by horses not racing in their true role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Tires, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Nightsinwhitesatin is pushed harder than expected in the early stages and fades badly inside the final 2f, creating a scramble finish among horses that have tracked midfield.
scenarios.body: High Fibre is the wild card here — a 645-day absentee (51 career jumps) dropping back to a flat context with Harry Fry's strong 14-day form (3/4); Secret Beach has prior form on Good at 12f and could be produced late if the pace collapses.

watchPoints.text: Watch Nightsinwhitesatin's early position — if anything forces Cian Horgan to go faster than intended in the first half-mile, her uncontested-pace advantage evaporates and the entire probability structure of this race shifts toward hold-up horses.

High Fibre is 645 days absent and returning from 51 hurdle starts — watch paddock condition and early pace; if he moves well pre-race and settles immediately off the leader, Harry Fry's strong recent form (3/4 in 14 days) makes him a live each-way price.

Pleasant Man has finished placed in four of his last six over this sort of trip on Good ground — watch whether Alex Jary gets him a position directly on Nightsinwhitesatin's heels from the outset, as that tracking berth is the key to his chance in Scenario B.

Green Sky's quick 7-day turnaround after a win deserves respect as a market signal — watch betting moves, as Millman connections running him back rapidly may indicate peak fitness, even though his natural style is compromised by the race shape.

Monitor the going report carefully — the 5:40 is listed as Good to Firm, which is a slight upgrade from the earlier races; if the ground is riding faster than the official description, the hold-up horses forced into midfield lose even more ground late and prominent runners gain further advantage.
